messages:
anya: Quick sync — debating gateway fanout (one private endpoint per tenant) vs a shared edge gateway with tenant routing. main concerns: operational complexity, IP/ENI scaling, cost, and debugging churn. any quick takes?
ben_p: Fanout wins on isolation + simpler per-tenant network policies. downside = ENI/IP explosion and higher NAT/eip costs. also harder to rollout infra changes.
cody: We ran a cost sim: 10k tenants with fanout (small endpoints) -> ~3.2k ENIs active avg, est $Xk/mo more than shared gateway. but tail latency improved for noisy tenants.
leah: For regulated customers we probably need fanout anyway (SLA + audit scope). question: can we auto-tier so only high-SLA tenants get fanout?
anya: exactly what I was thinking — hybrid. default -> shared gateway. opt-in reserved endpoint for customers who hit policy or SLA thresholds.
ben_p: Implementation caveat: shared gateway needs decent routing isolation (tenant id in SNI / mTLS SAN or header). we must avoid header-trust blowups.
cody: Another ops caveat: debugging cross-tenant noisy flows on shared gateway sucks. need better per-tenant observability (token-level traces) + sampling.
leah: Also consider 1) predictable IP pools per AZ for shared gateway to avoid AWS limits and 2) ephemeral extension for fanout during spikes (auto-provision ephemeral endpoints).
anya: +1 to ephemeral fanout for bursts rather than permanent per-tenant ENIs for every tenant. reduces steady-state cost.
ben_p: Edge case: DNS/tls termination. If we terminate TLS at shared gateway we lose tenant cert isolation unless we SNI-proxy. Per-tenant certs on fanout endpoints is simpler.
cody: Proposed rollout: 1) PRD for hybrid model, 2) implement telemetry + tenant routing on shared gateway, 3) add opt-in fanout and ephemeral lifecycles, 4) measure cost/latency.
anya: Sounds good. can someone spin up a spike to measure provisioning time for ephemeral endpoints and EIP allocation contention?
leah: I'll take the provisioning spike. ETA EOW.
ben_p: I'll draft a short RFC for hybrid model and the routing contract (SNI vs mTLS vs header). mention fallback semantics when fanout quota exhausted.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: created issue #2246 for provisioning spike and #2247 for RFC draft.
anya: Awesome — thanks. follow-up: we should add a small test harness to simulate noisy tenants hitting shared gateway to tune batch/conn limits.
leah: agreed, adding to the spike ticket.
anya: Cool. moving this to RFC prep channel when draft is ready. :thumbsup:
